description: The embedded REPORTS extension pack -- the opt-in, isolated report bundle: the four report namespaces (`source`/`period`/`audience`/`cadence`) plus the `type:report` rule that requires `source`/`period` on any document tagged `type:report`. Carries NO generic vocabulary (no required fields, no description caps, no file_class rules, no exempt entries) -- it is meant to be layered ON TOP of a base pack that supplies the `type` namespace (e.g. `default@1`), never used standalone. Layering this pack after that base pack overrides the base's inert report placeholder with this pack's real trigger/period -- a repo that does not need report semantics simply omits this pack from its `navigator.toml` extensions.

description_caps.source: This pack adds no description-cap classes -- classification is `default@1`'s job.

file_class.note: Matches `default@1`'s own `default` value so layering never triggers a spurious override warning; this pack adds no file_class rules of its own -- classification is `default@1`'s job.

namespaces.name: source
namespaces.source: The report's data-source axis -- report-only, required whenever `type:report` fires (see `report.required_namespaces`).

namespaces.name: period
namespaces.source: The report's covered calendar window -- report-only, required whenever `type:report` fires. `type: date_interval` -- a downstream range-eligibility consumer (facetquery) treats this facet's value as a closed date range and matches on OVERLAP against a query window, not equality.

namespaces.name: audience
namespaces.source: The report's intended consumer -- report-only, optional even when `type:report` fires.

namespaces.name: cadence
namespaces.source: The report's refresh frequency -- report-only, optional; defaults to on-demand when unspecified (NOT report-required).

report.notes: `cadence` defaults to on-demand when unspecified and is NOT required; `audience` is optional. `period` is `type: date_interval`, ISO 8601 interval form (`YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD`, single `/` separator, both endpoints inclusive). Uses explicit ASCII `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, because the Rust validator compiles this string with the `regex` crate, whose `\d` matches any Unicode decimal digit by default -- `[0-9]` is ASCII-only regardless of that flag, rejecting e.g. Arabic-Indic digits that an un-flagged Python `\d` would otherwise accept. This block expresses `report` in the current `core@1` shape (trigger/required_namespaces/period); `core@2` (M1.P3.T1) re-expresses it as a general `{match, apply}` rule-set with no code change here.
report.source: Salvaged from `frontmatter-psa-apm.pack.json`'s `report`/`namespaces` blocks (originally `schema.py:83-91` + `is_report:122-128` + `tag_rule_violations:180-191`) -- the real report semantics that pack's inert placeholder in `default@1` defers to this pack for.

exempt.source: This pack adds no exemptions -- the generated/exempt taxonomy is `default@1`'s job.
